issues.legal_issue: For the purpose of specific performance, an interest acquired by a seller after agreeing to sell property may be used to make good the contract even if no sale deed has yet been executed.
material_facts: The seller agreed to sell a house but could not convey the entire property because his mother also had an interest in it.
The buyer sued for specific performance after the seller failed to execute the sale deed.
While the appeal was pending, the mother died, and the seller acquired an interest in the portion of the house that had belonged to her.
The buyer sought specific performance as to the entire house.
issues.conclusion: The seller had to make good the agreement from the interest in the house acquired after the contract; the buyer was entitled to a sale deed for the entire house upon satisfying the payment condition imposed by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(a) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 applies where a person contracts to sell property with an imperfect title and later acquires an interest in it. The words “subsequently to the sale or lease” mean subsequently to the contract to sell or let, not subsequently to execution of the conveyance. The Court relied on Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar, [1954] S.C.R. 958, and reasoned that this reading fits the specific-performance provisions in sections 12–20, including sections 14–17, and avoids unnecessary overlap with section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act.

rule.if: specific_performance_claim and seller_contracted_to_sell and seller_had_imperfect_title and seller_later_acquired_interest

predicates.specific_performance_claim: A buyer sought judicial enforcement of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.seller_contracted_to_sell: The seller agreed to sell the property to the buyer.
predicates.seller_had_imperfect_title: When making the agreement, the seller had an interest in the property but could not convey the whole property with an unimpaired title.
predicates.seller_later_acquired_interest: After making the agreement, the seller acquired an additional interest in the property.
predicates.seller_must_make_good_contract_from_late: The seller must perform the agreement using the interest acquired after making it.

issues.definition: When a buyer seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property, the seller had an imperfect title at the time of contracting, and the seller later acquired an interest in the property, the seller must make good the agreement from that later-acquired interest.
